title: Late Breaking Results: A Geometric Diffusion Model for Macro Placement Generation
problem: Macro placement in VLSI design directly impacts circuit performance but remains a challenging optimization problem. Traditional approaches struggle to preserve circuit connectivity while satisfying placement constraints.
motivation: Macro placement is critical for circuit performance; generative approaches offer efficiency but must balance wirelength optimization with placement quality.
method: MacroDiff uses diffusion-based generative modeling (an iterative refinement technique, similar to progressively denoising an image) to place large circuit blocks called macros. Instead of directly predicting where each macro should go, it first predicts the wirelength relationships—how far signals need to travel between components. This indirect representation automatically preserves how signals connect through the circuit, reduces the number of placement constraints, and naturally handles rotations and translations (different orientations and positions of the layout).
key_novelty: By using wirelength relationships (distances signals need to travel between components) as an intermediate representation instead of direct placement coordinates, diffusion-based macro placement automatically preserves circuit connectivity and handles rotations and translations.
contributions: Diffusion-based generative model for macro placement
